definitions.explanation: A Japanese festival held on July 7th celebrating the annual meeting of the deities Orihime and Hikoboshi across the Milky Way.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}に{願|ねが}い{事|ごと}を{書|か}いた。
examples.english: I wrote a wish for Tanabata.

examples.japanese: {七夕|たなばた}は{七月七日|しちがつなのか}に{行|おこな}われる。
{子|こ}どもたちが{七夕|たなばた}の{飾|かざ}りを{作|つく}った。

notes:
ORIGIN:
{七夕|たなばた} originates from the Chinese Qixi Festival, combined with Japanese legends. The name literally means 'seventh evening.'

THE LEGEND:
The weaver princess {織姫|おりひめ} (represented by Vega) and the cowherd {彦星|ひこぼし} (represented by Altair) are lovers separated by the {天|あま}の{川|がわ} (Milky Way). They are allowed to meet only once a year on this night.

TRADITIONS:
- Writing wishes on {短冊|たんざく} (colored paper strips)
- Hanging decorations on bamboo branches ({笹|ささ})
- Making {七夕飾|たなばたかざ}り (Tanabata decorations)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {七夕祭|たなばたまつ}り: Tanabata festival
- {七夕飾|たなばたかざ}り: Tanabata decorations
- {七夕|たなばた}の{夜|よる}: the night of Tanabata

REGIONAL VARIATION:
In some regions (notably Sendai), Tanabata is celebrated on August 7th following the old lunar calendar.
